title: Coffee probability 2018 (Forest Data Partnership model 2026a)
description:
Per-pixel probability, from 0 to 1, that the pixel includes coffee in 2018, at 10 m resolution.

Coffee is a minor crop in this area and the reference database lists no coffee samples for Ghana or Côte d'Ivoire. Use this collection as a negative control next to cocoa, or to check for false positives, rather than as a coffee map.

Measured from the tiles' 2783 px overview level (about 40 m): tile means range from 0.000 to 0.026, with a median of 0.000, and 0 of 224 tiles have a mean of 0.1 or more.

The Forest Data Partnership (https://developers.google.com/earth-engine/datasets/publisher/forestdatapartnership) is a collaboration on global monitoring of deforestation, degradation and restoration linked to commodity production. It is coordinated with the FAO (https://www.fao.org/in-action/forest-data-partnership) and its reference data come from contributors such as the FAO, WRI, CIAT, MapBiomas, SERVIR, IIASA and Google. Google produces the community models: a deep learning model trained on the AlphaEarth Foundation annual satellite embeddings (64 features per 10 m pixel) with millions of community-sourced reference points. Release 2026a covers the pan-tropical belt from 24°S to 24°N for 2018, 2020, 2022 and 2024, and adds input data, bug fixes and a reworked processing pipeline over release 2025b. The maps are per-pixel probabilities, so users choose a threshold for their purpose, for example commodity supply-chain and deforestation-regulation checks. The datasets are not yet peer reviewed. Method and limitations: https://github.com/google/forest-data-partnership/tree/main/models/model_2026a

This collection mirrors the 224 one-degree tiles of release 2026a for 2018 that touch the West African cocoa belt: land in Sierra Leone, Liberia, Guinea, Côte d'Ivoire, Ghana, Togo, Benin, Nigeria, Cameroon, Equatorial Guinea and Gabon south of 10°N, between 15°W and 17°E and between 1°S and 11°N. The files are copied unchanged from Google's requester-pays bucket, byte for byte, and each item records Google's MD5 for the file. Each tile is one item with one Cloud-Optimized GeoTIFF of about 11133 by 11133 Float32 pixels in EPSG:4326. The same tiles exist for cocoa, coffee, oil palm and rubber, with identical item ids, and for each mirrored year.

overview.title: Coffee probability 2018, pan-tropical overview at about 320 m (COG)
overview.description: All 5516 tiles of release 2026a for 2018 (24°S to 24°N), not only the tiles this collection mirrors, in one file at about 320 m: the 347 px level of every source tile as Google published it (mean-resampled), mosaicked without resampling again. NaN where no tile or no data. For maps below zoom 9 and coarse statistics.

overview.processing:lineage: For each of the release's source tiles: gdal_translate -ovr 4 (the 347 px internal overview, as published, unchanged). Then gdalbuildvrt -vrtnodata nan over the extracts, and gdal_translate -of COG -co COMPRESS=ZSTD -co PREDICTOR=YES -co BLOCKSIZE=512 -co OVERVIEW_RESAMPLING=AVERAGE -co STATISTICS=YES. Script: tools/build_overview.sh.
